findings.finding: Unexpected English reply asks for a previous question instead of answering the current explicit question.
Uses an earlier historical scheme instead of the requested event-date version.
Claims the requested later record is absent although it exists later in the source.
Background paraphrase does not preserve the distinction between a party misunderstanding another party and holding that position itself.
One sentence shifts a requested addition into wording suggesting it has already been added.
Adds causal and ordering interpretation between source statements without consistently labeling it as inference.
Says the earlier date contains only one item, overlooking the continuation across a page boundary; adds an unnecessary year extrapolation.
Ancillary source-range summary assigns a later-year record to the earlier year.
